newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks rise to new record high at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks rise to new record high at open.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks climbed further into uncharted territory at the open after U.S. economic data again came in below expectations. * 7.76 million shares traded worth C$117 million.
Toronto stocks climbed further into uncharted territory at the open on Friday after U.S. economic data again came in below market expectations.
Traders said gains were made across the board, with the exception of golds, which fell slightly on weak bullion.
"I think the economic numbers were obviously better than expected and that got the bonds started early, and it looks like we've got more of the same continuing," one trader said.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 12.15 points to 6527.76 in turnover of 7.8 million shares.
Total trading value was C$117 million.
Advancing stocks outnumbered declines 234 to 171, while 217 issues were flat.
Economists said lower than expected Friday U.S. PPI and Thursday U.S. retail sales data reduced the likelihood that the Federal Reserve would hike interest rates at its next meeting on July 1-2.
Ten of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes were higher, led by utilities, banks and paper and forest products.
The trader said the interest-sensitive banks and utilities should continue to benefit from decreased rate-hike fears.

"We've had continued good strength in the utility stocks since the rates. It appears they're not going to be increasing them at all...the banks are all doing better across the board. They opened firmer and I'd expect them to stay strong most of the day," the trader said.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Shares in Teleglobe Inc rose 2.10 to 48.50 in moderate trade after the overseas telephone communications carrier said on Thursday it expected its net profit to increase by 20 percent in 1997.
* Inco Ltd's Voisey Bay Nickel Co shares fell 0.65 to 29.50 in active trade after the nickel giant said on Thursday the environmental permit process in Labrador was behind schedule.
